name: Porokeratosis of Mibelli

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and histopathological criteria for Porokeratosis of Mibelli

criteria.description: Presence of annular plaques with raised keratotic border and central atrophy
Histological identification of cornoid lamella in skin biopsy
Lesions typically localized on extremities and trunk with centrifugal expansion
Positive family history suggestive of autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesions plus histopathological confirmation of cornoid lamella
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; genetic testing is not routinely performed.

other: Skin biopsy showing cornoid lamella is diagnostic
Lesions demonstrate clonal proliferation of abnormal keratinocytes

distinguishingFeatures: Actinic keratosis lacks cornoid lamella histologically
Usually occurs on sun-exposed areas in elderly
Lesions are typically scaly macules or papules without raised keratotic border
Multiple small superficial lesions rather than large plaques

redFlags: Rapid enlargement or ulceration of lesion suggesting malignant transformation
Persistent pain or bleeding from lesions
references: James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
Bolognia JL, Schaffer JV, Cerroni L. Dermatology. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2018.
